top_events.title: Attacks Cut Saudi Oil Output and East-West Pipeline Flow, State News Agency Says - EnergyNow.com

analysis.summary: Reported attacks cut Saudi oil output and reduced East-West pipeline flow, indicating a potentially material Saudi supply and transportation disruption. This would generally support crude prices, though the duration and extent are not provided.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices can support Exxon Mobil’s upstream earnings and cash flow, although broader geopolitical and operational risks remain uncertain.

top_events.title: Attacks Cut Saudi Oil Output and East-West Pipeline Flow, State News Agency Says - energynow.com

analysis.summary: A state news agency reports that attacks reduced Saudi oil output and disrupted East-West pipeline flows, implying a potential near-term tightening of crude supply and transport capacity. No outage magnitude or duration is provided.
analysis.why_xom: Higher crude prices could support Exxon Mobil's upstream earnings and cash flow. The effect is not unambiguously positive because broader regional disruption could also raise operating and logistics risks, but the direct crude-price signal is bullish.

top_events.title: OPEC+ Approves Further Oil Output Increase as Hormuz Exports Start to Recover - EnergyNow

analysis.summary: The headline indicates two potentially bearish developments for crude: OPEC+ approved an additional output increase, and oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz are beginning to recover. Together, these imply improved available supply and reduced disruption risk.
analysis.why_xom: Lower crude prices or reduced geopolitical supply-risk premiums could pressure Exxon Mobil’s upstream earnings, though the headline provides no detail on the size or timing of the output increase or export recovery.

top_events.title: Hormuz at Near Standstill as Iran Warns Ships to Keep to its Waters - EnergyNow.com

analysis.summary: The headline reports that Strait of Hormuz shipping is near a standstill after Iran warned vessels to remain in Iranian waters, implying a potentially significant disruption at a major crude transit chokepoint. The report does not quantify volumes or confirm a formal closure.
analysis.why_xom: A sustained Hormuz shipping disruption could support global crude prices, benefiting XOM's upstream earnings. Effects on XOM's refining and logistics operations are less certain, so the net company impact is assessed as bullish but not definitive.

analysis.summary: The headline reports both an additional OPEC+ output increase and recovering oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, implying improved supply availability and potential downward pressure on crude prices.
analysis.why_xom: Lower crude prices can weigh on Exxon Mobil's upstream earnings and cash flow, although the headline provides no details on the size, timing, or implementation of the output increase or the extent of Hormuz export recovery.

log_health.last_line: 2026-09-19 09:41:18,999 | INFO | feed updated | new=12 active=249 signal=+0.711 adjustment=+7.10

review.summary: Decision coverage is substantial, but execution and outcome evidence is absent. The model produced 4,154 HOLD and 2 BUY decisions, with both BUY actions in TSLA, yet no orders, fills, trade rows, or realized trades were recorded. Score extrema crossed configured thresholds for several symbols, but the supplied aggregates cannot show crossing frequency, confirmation persistence, position eligibility, or blocking reasons. The dashboard and geo snapshots are not aligned to the 2026-09-25 review date, limiting causal interpretation. No threshold, VIX, geo, or exit calibration is supported today.
findings: Observed: 4,154 of 4,156 decisions were HOLD (99.952%); 2 were BUY (0.048%), both for TSLA. There were no SELL decisions.
Observed: TSLA's action-level BUY rate was 2 of 461 rows (0.434%). Every other symbol had zero BUY and SELL actions.

Observed: AMZN, NVDA, and TSLA had maximum scores above the 70 buy threshold. NVDA, TSLA, and XOM had minimum scores below the 30 sell threshold. Aggregate extrema do not reveal the number or duration of threshold crossings, and therefore do not establish whether the two-confirmation requirement was met.
Observed: No orders, fills, trade CSV rows, or realized-trade rows were recorded. Realized P/L of zero reflects the absence of realized records and is not evidence of flat model performance.

Observed: The two TSLA BUY decisions did not become recorded orders. Hypothesis: they may have been blocked by confirmation, portfolio, session, duplicate-order, or other eligibility controls, but no rejection-reason evidence is supplied.
Observed: Average scores varied moderately by symbol, from 47.825 for AMZN to 51.865 for TSLA. One day without executions or forward-return labels cannot support per-symbol threshold changes.

Observed: Average VIX adjustments ranged from -0.176 for GLD to +0.500 for TSLA. The only supplied VIX level, 14.87, comes from a dashboard generated after the review date, so VIX effects cannot be linked reliably to the 2026-09-25 decisions.

Observed: Average geo adjustment was 0.0 for every symbol, including XOM, while the available geo artifact reported a +7.1 adjustment. That artifact was generated on 2026-09-19, six days before the review date, and contains apparent duplicate coverage of the same headlines across domain variants.

Observed: The geo feed's average model contribution cannot be evaluated from this day because no decision row shows a nonzero geo adjustment. Hypothesis: a freshness or applicability gate may have correctly suppressed the stale artifact, but the supplied data does not identify the reason.

Observed: The dashboard snapshot was generated on 2026-09-27 rather than the 2026-09-25 review date. It showed 5 open positions and $12,575.46 exposure versus configured caps of 4 positions and $10,000. Because of the date mismatch and possible market-value appreciation, this does not prove that a same-day order breached a cap.

Observed: The later dashboard's five positions had market values slightly above $2,500 each. This alone does not prove violation of the $2,500 entry-notional limit because market values can rise after entry.

Observed: Buy/sell balance, realized profitability, stop-loss behavior, take-profit behavior, and trailing-stop behavior cannot be assessed without orders, fills, exits, and time-aligned position history.

proposals.title: Add a decision-to-order funnel with explicit gate reasons
proposals.target: Decision audit records and paper-order submission pipeline
proposals.current: Decision rows contain final actions, but the evidence does not expose raw threshold-cross events, confirmation counters, position eligibility, cap checks, market-session checks, or reasons why a BUY did not create an order.
proposals.proposed: For every non-HOLD candidate and every raw score crossing, log symbol, side, score, threshold, consecutive-confirmation count, current position state, projected paper exposure, open-position count, market-session state, final disposition, and a single enumerated gate reason. Record paper-order attempt and acceptance identifiers separately. Do not alter thresholds or execution behavior.
evidence: Two TSLA BUY decisions were recorded, but orders and fills were both zero.
AMZN, NVDA, and TSLA exceeded the buy threshold by daily maximum, while only TSLA produced BUY actions.
NVDA, TSLA, and XOM fell below the sell threshold by daily minimum, while no SELL action was recorded.
proposals.risk: Low operational risk; added logging volume and schema changes must avoid disrupting the one-minute decision loop or exposing unsanitized data.

proposals.title: Enforce and audit paper portfolio-cap invariants before every BUY
proposals.target: Paper portfolio reconciliation and pre-order risk gate
proposals.current: Configured limits are 4 open positions and $10,000 total exposure, while a later dashboard snapshot reports 5 positions and $12,575.46 exposure. The available timestamps cannot determine whether this resulted from legacy state, appreciation, reconciliation drift, or an order-gate defect.
proposals.proposed: Before any paper BUY submission, reconcile paper positions and open orders, calculate projected position count and projected exposure, and reject the order if either configured cap would be exceeded. Emit an invariant-violation event at startup and each cycle when existing state is already above a cap. Keep the dashboard read-only and preserve all existing caps, daily-loss controls, and paper=True.
evidence: Configured max_open_positions is 4 and max_total_exposure is $10,000.
The 2026-09-27 dashboard reports 5 positions and $12,575.46 exposure.
No same-day order records are available to identify the source of the discrepancy.
proposals.risk: Stale or incomplete position reconciliation could conservatively block valid paper entries; the guard must fail closed without liquidating or modifying existing paper positions automatically.

proposals.title: Add geo-feed freshness, deduplication, and application diagnostics
proposals.target: Geo-feed ingestion and score-adjustment audit fields
proposals.current: The geo artifact is six days older than the review date, reports a +7.1 adjustment and 249 active events, and includes apparent duplicate stories. Decision aggregates show a 0.0 geo adjustment for every symbol without explaining whether the feed was stale, inapplicable, or unavailable.
proposals.proposed: In SHADOW, canonicalize article URL/domain/title fingerprints, report raw versus deduplicated event counts, record feed age, and attach an enumerated geo-application status to each decision. Add a configurable freshness limit that quarantines stale geo data from scoring while still logging its counterfactual adjustment. Do not activate the supplied +7.1 adjustment or change trading thresholds.
evidence: The feed reports signal 0.7105 and score adjustment 7.1, but all symbols show average geo adjustment 0.0.
Multiple top events repeat the same publication time and headline through domain or capitalization variants.
proposals.risk: Over-aggressive deduplication could merge genuinely distinct reports; shadow comparison should precede any production scoring effect.

proposals.title: Collect per-symbol threshold and VIX outcome cohorts before calibration
proposals.current: The evidence provides score aggregates and average VIX adjustments but no crossing counts, persistence, forward returns, counterfactual exits, or time-aligned volatility regimes.
proposals.proposed: For each raw buy or sell threshold crossing, record symbol, side, score distance from threshold, confirmation outcome, VIX level and change, geo freshness status, and forward paper returns at 5, 15, and 60 minutes and market close. Keep blocked signals as counterfactual observations. Require at least 12 eligible observations in a defined symbol-side or pooled regime cohort before considering calibration; make no threshold or VIX-weight changes now.
evidence: Only two final BUY actions and zero SELL actions occurred.
There are no orders, fills, or realized outcomes.
Average VIX adjustments differ by symbol, but the available VIX snapshot is not time-aligned with the review day.
proposals.risk: Forward-return research can suffer from missing bars, overlapping observations, and selection bias; results must remain paper-only and should not be treated as causal without adequate cohorts.

proposals.title: Make review artifacts date-scoped and freshness-aware
proposals.target: Daily review data assembly and dashboard snapshot metadata
proposals.current: The review is dated 2026-09-25, but the dashboard snapshot is from 2026-09-27 and the geo snapshot is from 2026-09-19. These artifacts are presented alongside same-day decisions without an explicit as-of eligibility status.
proposals.proposed: Join artifacts by review date and market timezone, retain source generated_at timestamps, and label each artifact as in-window, stale, or future relative to the review cutoff. Exclude out-of-window dashboard state from same-day portfolio and VIX conclusions while preserving it in a clearly labeled diagnostics section. Keep the dashboard read-only.
proposals.risk: Strict date filtering may temporarily reduce report coverage when snapshots are delayed, but it prevents misleading same-day attribution.
